UI_THEME.description: UI color theme: dark or light. Applies appliance-wide, not per-browser.

POLLING_MODE.description: continuous (always polling) or time_limited (default -- runs for POLLING_DURATION_HOURS, then pauses until manually resumed via Start Now).

POLLING_DURATION_HOURS.description: How many hours a time-limited polling run lasts before pausing. Only used when POLLING_MODE is time_limited.

_POLLING_ACTIVE.description: Internal flag: whether the poller is currently doing work (vs. paused after a time-limited run ended).

_POLLING_STARTED_AT.description: Internal timestamp of the current polling run's start, used to compute when a time-limited run has elapsed.

_POLLING_PAUSED_AT.description: Internal timestamp of when the current pause began, used to drive the Settings page's live 'Paused for HH:MM:SS' counter.

SCAN_INTERFACE_OVERRIDE.description: Network interface name (e.g. eth2) to scope discovery to, instead of the OS's own default route. Empty = today's behavior, unaffected. For multi-homed appliances (a separate NIC for the network actually under test). Linux only for now. Takes effect on the next tick -- no restart needed.

SNMP_COMMUNITY_STRING.description: The default SNMP v2c community string used to query infrastructure.

SNMP_TRY_PUBLIC_COMMUNITY.description: Also try the well-known default SNMP community string 'public' if your configured strings fail. Disable on networks where this default has been intentionally removed, to avoid tripping intrusion-detection alerts for repeated default-credential attempts. Except where used for security alerting -- see SNMP_SECURITY_SCAN_PUBLIC, controlled separately.

SNMP_SECURITY_SCAN_PUBLIC.description: Actively check whether 'public' also works on devices that already have a different working SNMP credential, so a device vulnerable to both isn't missed just because its real credential was found first. Independent of SNMP_TRY_PUBLIC_COMMUNITY -- disabling that setting to avoid intrusion-detection alerts does not disable this security check; disable this one separately if you don't want it either.

IEEE_OUI_URL.description: The upstream source URL for the daily IEEE MAC-to-Vendor registry.

HTTP_USER_AGENT.value: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64; rv:128.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/128.0
HTTP_USER_AGENT.description: The User-Agent string Netlanvas uses when making external web requests.

WIFI_STRICT_MODE.description: Require strict 802.11 MIBs to map Wi-Fi clients.

DB_ARCHIVE_ON_BOOT.description: Testing Mode: Archive and purge the SQLite database on every container restart.

SETUP_COMPLETE.description: Internal flag indicating if the first-time setup flow is finished.

LOGIN_COUNT.description: Tracks UI dashboard load frequency for lifecycle events.

IS_REGISTERED.description: Has this Netlanvas instance opted-in and registered with the community cloud?

SUBMIT_TELEMETRY.description: Allow additional, more detailed anonymous usage telemetry. A separate, minimal anonymous install-count ping (random ID only, no other data) is always sent regardless of this setting -- see the note near Instance ID below.

SESSION_LIFETIME_HOURS.description: How long a login session remains valid before requiring re-authentication.

TLS_VALIDITY_DAYS.description: Validity period, in days, for the self-signed TLS certificate generated at first boot.

TLS_RENEW_WITHIN_DAYS.description: Reissue the self-signed TLS certificate automatically when fewer than this many days remain before expiry.

AUTO_UPDATE_APP.description: Automatically pull and apply new NetLanvas releases as they're published, without waiting for you to click Update Now. Base infrastructure (redis/caddy) always updates automatically regardless of this setting.

IEEE_OUI28_URL.description: The upstream source URL for IEEE's MA-M (28-bit) registry -- newer/smaller vendor blocks not covered by the classic MA-L oui.txt.

IEEE_OUI36_URL.description: The upstream source URL for IEEE's MA-S (36-bit) registry -- same purpose as IEEE_OUI28_URL, for the even smaller/newer vendor blocks.

IANA_ENTERPRISE_NUMBERS_URL.description: The upstream source URL for IANA private-enterprise-numbers.txt -- resolves a device SNMP sysObjectID to a vendor name, independent of MAC (works even on locally-administered/randomized MACs where OUI lookup cannot).
